g.text: N52 Review Read-Aloud (Owner Reads Real Reviews)
g.textArea:
What it is: The owner, founder or an expert host sits with a tablet/laptop (selfie or podcast set) and goes through real customer reviews or customer-submitted before/after photos one at a time, each shown on screen as a screenshot/photo card, reading them aloud and reacting/explaining; often opens by addressing a skeptic ('these positive reviews are all bought!') and closes with the guarantee and link. Usually long (1-5 min).

Why it works: Turns a pile of reviews into a personal, believable walkthrough that answers 'are these real?' head-on; best for warm/retargeting audiences and products with lots of strong written reviews or customer photos.

How to make one: 1) Open on the objection: read a skeptical comment ('your reviews are fake') or tease 'let's look at what you sent us'. 2) Sit with a tablet and read 5-10 real reviews (or react to before/after photos) one by one, overlaying each as a Trustpilot/review screenshot and adding a short comment on each. 3) Close by restating the guarantee ('if it doesn't work you get your money back') and pointing to the link.

Closest format already on the board: UGC Testimonial Mashup [BOF] - that cuts together clips of customers speaking; here no customer appears, the owner/host reads their written reviews or photos aloud and reacts to each.

What it is: The brand opens by admitting a public mistake ('We f*cked up our spring sale'), proves it with a screen recording of the error and screenshots of angry/mocking customer comments, then 'makes it right' with an even bigger discount + free gifts and closes on urgency ('before we sell out').

Why it works: Self-deprecating honesty stops the scroll and the apology gives a believable reason for an unusually big discount.

How to make one: 1) Pick a real or plausible slip (wrong % live, typo, shipping delay) and open with a blunt confession caption. 2) Show proof: screen recording of the mistake + 3-5 customer comment screenshots roasting you. 3) Pivot to the make-good offer (bigger discount, gifts) with product b-roll and a sell-out urgency close.

Closest format already on the board: Reply To Question / Personal Update - here the hook is the brand's own public mistake and comment backlash, used as the reason-why for a sale.
